observations: Invented model fixes wage one hundred thousand with degree and fifty without; earning costs twenty for high-productivity type and sixty for other type.
Initial net pay eighty versus fifty and forty versus fifty led only high-productivity workers to obtain the degree.
Reducing others' cost to forty led everyone to obtain it; raising both costs to sixty led no one to obtain it.
Screenshot shows cost segments and net-pay comparisons. Reveal explains initial separation, cheap-signal failure and explicitly says real degrees are not claimed to teach nothing.

complexity.reason: Requires net payoff and selection reasoning.

whyCool: A credential can reveal information because of who finds it worthwhile to earn, even if the credential itself adds no productivity in the model.
caveat: Fixed wage offer and invented types/costs; no wage-adjustment equilibrium or empirical education estimate.
